notes: Handoff state is now local-first (.dev-files/objectives/<id>/handoffs/) with the GitHub issue Resume block as an optional mirror, across five platforms. Evals 1-3 preserve the original three-platform issue-based behaviour (backward compatibility). Evals 4-6 cover the additions: Gemini/OpenCode targets, gh-less operation, and objective/task selectors.

evals.prompt: /switch-dev handoff #42 — I'm rate limited on Claude, switching to Cursor for the UI work. Branch is feat/auth-ui and worktree is .claude/.worktrees/feat-auth-ui.
evals.expected_output: Writes a local handoff record, mirrors it to issue #42's Resume block, sets agent:cursor, posts the handoff comment, and prints a copy-paste resume prompt for Cursor. Warns if commits are unpushed. Writes no code.
expectations: A handoff record is written locally before the GitHub mirror is attempted
update-issue-resume.sh (or gh) is used to update issue #42's Resume block
The target label is agent:cursor, matching the user's stated intent
Unpushed commits are pushed, or the user is warned they will be invisible
Prior Done items are appended to, never erased
A continuation prompt for Cursor is printed
No code is written and no PR is merged
The legacy .claude/.worktrees/ path is accepted without complaint

evals.expected_output: Loads state — local handoff record first, issue Resume as a mirror — resolves the worktree for the recorded branch, claims the agent label for the current platform, and prints the continuation checklist. Stops if the state reports a blocker.
expectations: Local objective/handoff state is consulted before or alongside the issue
parse-issue-resume.sh or gh issue view is used for the mirror
resolve-worktree.sh is used rather than a hardcoded .claude/ path
If local state and the issue disagree, local state and git are preferred and the choice is stated
Execution stops when Blocked/status is not none
The Next item is printed clearly
Delivery is not implied — resuming a task does not open a PR

evals.expected_output: Read-only dashboard: local objectives with their task statuses, agent-labelled issues when gh is available, and active worktrees, in a table.
expectations: Local .dev-files/objectives/ are listed with task states
Agent-labelled issues are listed when gh works, and the absence of gh is reported rather than failing
list-agent-worktrees.sh or git worktree list is used
Nothing is modified

evals.expected_output: Parses objective, task and target platform; writes .dev-files/objectives/auth-system/handoffs/task-002.json against the handoff schema; checks Gemini CLI's capabilities and names any degradation; prints a Gemini-targeted resume prompt. No GitHub issue is required.
expectations: parse-mode-args.sh resolves objective=auth-system, task-002 and target gemini
The handoff record is written to .dev-files/objectives/auth-system/handoffs/task-002.json
commits and validation entries reflect what actually ran, not aspirations
The target platform's capabilities are checked and any degradation is stated
The flow completes without a GitHub issue number
The provider (gemini) does not appear in the branch name or worktree path

assertions.text: gemini is accepted as a target platform
No branch or path in the output contains the provider name

evals.prompt: /switch-dev handoff — continuing this on OpenCode later. There's no GitHub remote on this repo.
evals.expected_output: Completes entirely on local state: writes the handoff record, states in one line that the GitHub mirror was skipped because there is no remote/gh, and prints an OpenCode-targeted resume prompt. Does not treat the missing mirror as a failure.
expectations: The handoff record is written locally
The missing GitHub mirror is reported in one line and does not abort the handoff
opencode is recognised as a target platform
OpenCode-specific degradations (no Claude hooks, no statusline) are not assumed away

assertions.text: The handoff completes successfully with no gh calls succeeding

evals.expected_output: Loads the objective, lists its tasks and their statuses, identifies the next actionable task (dependencies satisfied, status ready), resolves its worktree, and prints the continuation checklist for that task.
expectations: objective.json and tasks/*.json are read
The next actionable task is chosen by dependency satisfaction, not by file order alone
A worktree/branch is resolved for that task
The output names the objective, the task, and the next step

evals.prompt: /switch-dev status — gh is not installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: Capability fallback case. The dashboard is produced from local .dev-files/objectives/ state and git worktrees alone. The unavailable GitHub listing is reported in one line as degraded, not as an error, and the mode still completes.
expectations: Local objectives and task statuses are listed without any successful gh call
The unsupported GitHub listing is reported in one line and does not abort the mode
list-agent-worktrees.sh or git worktree list still runs
Nothing is modified
The output does not present an empty GitHub section as though no work exists
